AR.name: Caña brava
AR.citation: SIB (Sistema de Informacion de Biodiversidad), Parques Nacionales, Argentina - official species profile: 'Arundo donax (cana hueca, cana de Castilla, cana brava)'. Also documented via ArgentiNat (iNaturalist Argentina national node). Listed among the world's 100 worst invasive species.

CL.name: Cañabrava
CL.citation: Chile's official Ministerio de Medio Ambiente iNaturalist portal (inaturalist.mma.gob.cl): 'La cana comun, cana de Castilla, carrizo, chin, canavera o canabrava (Arundo donax)'.

ES.name: Caña
ES.citation: Medir S.L. (cane/reed manufacturer for wind instruments); long documented use across the Mediterranean, though genuinely ancient/native status vs. very early introduction remains debated. Used to craft traditional wind instruments such as the Spanish dulzaina

FR.name: Canne de Provence
FR.citation: Ask-Ayurveda historical review; used to craft the traditional Provencal galoubet wind instrument

MX.name: Carrizo
MX.citation: iNaturalist; also documented as the name used along the Colorado River region shared with the southwestern US

US.name: Giant reed
US.citation: US Forest Service Research and Development (FEIS species review). Also documented as Spanish cane, giant cane, Colorado river reed. The principal source material worldwide for reeds used in woodwind instruments (oboe, bassoon, clarinet, saxophone). SAFETY/ECOLOGY: listed among the world's 100 worst invasive alien species; a major riparian-corridor threat in southern California
